newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, Anglo still discussing sale of Lonrho stake.
newsitem.headline: EU, Anglo still discussing sale of Lonrho stake.

text.p: The European Commission is still studying whether to allow mining giant Anglo American Corp of South Africa to sell part of its stake in Lonrho Plc to JCI Ltd, another South African mining firm.
A Commission source said the EU's competition services had had "technical discussions with the parties concerned", including apparently JCI chairman Mzi Khumalo.
But he would not speculate on when the Commission might take a final decision.

The Commission ordered Anglo American in April to reduce its holding in Lonrho, a British-based trading and mining firm, to 9.99 percent from 27.5 percent to avoid the two companies taking joint control of the platinum market.
The EU decision made it clear that the purchaser of the shares must be unrelated to Anglo.
JCI has taken an option to buy 26.8 percent of Lonrho from Anglo and De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd.
The Commission is looking closely into the deal because of Anglo's representation on the JCI board and the fact that Khumalo is an Anglo director.
Its July decision was based on EU merger control law which bans creation or strengthening of dominant positions in the European market, no matter where the companies involved are based.
